articles.title: 'A lonely road': Catherine joins cancer support group in new documentary
articles.summary: The documentary features her personal thoughts on her illness and recovery, following her cancer diagnosis.
articles.body:
The Princess of Wales is seen joining a cancer support group in newly-released footage from a forthcoming documentary called Heal.

"I haven't really explored this outside my family walls," Catherine tells a group of people from Shine Cancer Support.

The documentary features her personal thoughts on her illness and recovery.

Catherine has never disclosed what type of cancer she faced, but in March 2024 she revealed that she had a diagnosis of cancer and was receiving chemotherapy.

In January 2025 she said that she was in remission and in the following months began a gradual return to royal duties.

Heal will be shown on BBC iPlayer from 12:00 GMT and BBC One at 18:40 GMT on 29 November. It will also air internationally, including on NBCUniversal in the US on 30 November, Channel 9 in Australia on 1 December and CTV and Noovo in Canada on 7 December

articles.title: Árvore de Natal de crochê de 9 metros decora cidade no RS | G1
articles.standfirst: Grupo de cerca de 50 voluntárias de Campinas do Sul produziu mais de 6 mil quadrados de lã. Após as festas, material será higienizado e transformado em roupas e cobertores.
articles.summary: A árvore de Natal de crochê de 9 metros em Campinas do Sul mobilizou 50 voluntárias e terá seus 6 mil quadrados de lã transformados em cobertores após as festas.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Um grupo de cerca de 50 mulheres de Campinas do Sul , na região Norte do Rio Grande do Sul, construiu uma árvore de Natal de nove metros de altura feita inteiramente de crochê .

O projeto, que levou cerca de seis meses para ser concluído , utilizou mais de seis mil quadrados manuais de lã para decorar o centro da cidade para as festas de fim de ano.

O trabalho uniu artesãs e voluntárias do município. A professora de artesanato Marivone Anholeto Pegoraro explica que os pequenos pedaços de crochê foram costurados formando mantas, que depois foram unidas como um quebra-cabeça.

"Ela foi dividida em três partes porque a estrutura seria muito grande. E depois nós fizemos uma parte, depois a outra e, no fim, as três", detalha.

A doméstica Marlene Baldiga lembra que o projeto começou pequeno, mas logo ganhou a adesão da comunidade . Ela comemora a reação dos moradores. "Todo mundo que passa, ontem passou gente ali e disse, mas vocês que fizeram? Eu disse, sim, fomos nós que fizemos."

Os quadrados de crochê que sobraram da montagem do pinheiro foram espalhados pela praça para complementar a decoração natalina.

Além de enfeitar a cidade, os encontros para a produção da árvore criaram uma rede de apoio entre as participantes. A agricultora Ivone Balbinot Perim percorria nove quilômetros para costurar com o grupo.

"Eu vinha de carona com o filho que trabalha na cidade e depois eu voltava com uma amiga ou com a 'profe' até a Linha Paris e ainda fazia uns três quilômetros a pé, pra ir até em casa. Mas porque valia a pena vir participar dos encontros. Eu amo crochê", conta.

A primeira-dama de Campinas do Sul, Daniela Ciapparini Battisti, destaca que a proposta também buscou resgatar tradições familiares. "Essa era uma maneira também de nós resgatar os momentos com nossas avós. Hoje se fala muito em criar memórias, mas com isso também nós resgatamos muitas memórias", explica.

O projeto terá continuidade após o Natal. A lã utilizada na árvore e na decoração da praça será reaproveitada nos meses mais frios do ano . "A nossa expectativa é de higienizá-los depois e transformar em roupas, em cobertas, porque a lã é toda de altíssima qualidade. E aí nós reaproveitar", concluiu a primeira-dama.

articles.title: IBGE: planos de saúde custam R$ 528 por mês às famílias paulistas, 66% acima da média nacional | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisa aponta que gasto médio mensal familiar com plano ou seguro saúde em São Paulo supera em R$ 210 média do país; no estado, despesa total com saúde chega a R$ 1.001 por mês.
articles.summary: Pesquisa aponta que gasto médio mensal familiar com plano ou seguro saúde em São Paulo supera em R$ 210 média do país; no estado, despesa total com saúde chega a R$ 1.001 por mês.
articles.body:
Impacto econômico da saúde na vida do brasileiro — Foto: Mateus Andre | magnific.com

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

As famílias de São Paulo gastaram, em média, R$ 528,36 por mês com planos e seguros de saúde em 2024 e 2025 , segundo dados da Pesquisa de Orçamentos Familiares (POF) 2024-2025, divulgada pelo IBGE. O valor é 66% maior do que a média nacional , de R$ 318,05.

O dado faz parte do recorte estadual da pesquisa e mostra que o desembolso com assistência privada à saúde pesa mais no orçamento paulista do que no restante do país.

No total, a despesa média mensal das famílias paulistas com assistência à saúde foi de R$ 1.001,99, também acima da média brasileira, de R$ 765,71.

Na prática, isso significa que, em São Paulo, mais da metade do gasto familiar com saúde vai para plano ou seguro saúde. Dos R$ 1.001,99 gastos por mês nessa área, R$ 528,36 correspondem a esse item.

A categoria inclui os gastos das famílias com planos e seguros de saúde privados, dentro do grupo maior de assistência à saúde, que também reúne despesas com remédios, consultas, exames, internações, cirurgias e tratamento dentário.

Os dados do IBGE mostram que a saúde tem peso relevante no orçamento das famílias do estado. Em São Paulo, a assistência à saúde respondeu por 13,1% das despesas de consumo das famílias, o quarto maior gasto. No Brasil, essa participação foi de 12,1%.

As despesas de consumo são os gastos feitos diretamente para atender às necessidades e desejos dos moradores, como alimentação, habitação, transporte, saúde e educação.

Em São Paulo, os principais grupos de despesa de consumo foram:

O levantamento também mostra que o gasto com plano de saúde sobe de forma acentuada conforme aumenta a faixa de renda da família. Entre as famílias paulistas com rendimento total e variação patrimonial mensal de até R$ 3.036, a despesa média mensal com plano ou seguro saúde foi de R$ 73,05.

Mais de R$ 9.108 a R$ 15.180: R$ 548,02;

Mais de R$ 15.180 a R$ 22.770: R$ 921,65;

Mais de R$ 22.770 a R$ 37.950: R$ 1.418,97;

Na faixa mais alta, o gasto médio com plano de saúde é quase 45 vezes maior do que entre as famílias de menor renda.

Apesar disso, mesmo entre os mais pobres há desembolso com esse item, o que indica que o gasto com saúde suplementar não está restrito apenas às camadas mais ricas.

Além dos planos, os remédios também têm peso importante no orçamento de saúde das famílias paulistas. Em São Paulo, a despesa média mensal familiar com medicamentos foi de R$ 248,98 , acima da média brasileira, de R$ 214,92.

Outros gastos médios mensais das famílias paulistas com saúde foram:

Consulta e tratamento dentário: R$ 24,03

Tratamento médico e ambulatorial: R$ 19,62

Paulistas gastam mais do que a média do país

A pesquisa também mostra que o orçamento das famílias de São Paulo é maior do que o registrado nacionalmente. Segundo o IBGE, a despesa total média mensal familiar no estado foi de R$ 9.933,63, enquanto o gasto no Brasil foi de R$ 7.977,43, em média.

Já o rendimento total e a variação patrimonial médios mensais familiares chegaram a R$ 11.572,66 em São Paulo, contra R$ 9.255,53 na média nacional.

No estado, o rendimento do trabalho respondeu por R$ 7.408,10 mensais, também acima da média brasileira, de R$ 5.447,23.

A habitação consome 33,3% das despesas de consumo, acima dos 31,6% do Brasil;

O transporte responde por 16,8%, praticamente em linha com os 16,7% nacionais;

A alimentação pesa 15,9%, abaixo dos 17,7% da média brasileira;

A saúde fica em 13,1%, acima dos 12,1% do país.

A Pesquisa de Orçamentos Familiares é feita pelo IBGE para medir como as famílias brasileiras ganham e gastam dinheiro. A edição 2024-2025 coletou informações entre novembro de 2024 e novembro de 2025.

Segundo o instituto, os dados divulgados nesta etapa tratam principalmente de despesas, rendimentos e variação patrimonial.

No caso de São Paulo, os números mostram um orçamento familiar acima da média brasileira, mas também indicam que itens como moradia, transporte, alimentação e saúde privada exercem pressão importante sobre as contas das famílias.

articles.title: Black Friday Teresina: Consumidora viaja 40 km por bicicleta | G1
articles.standfirst: A Black Friday movimenta o comércio com consumidores em busca de promoções em Teresina; ferramentas ajudam a identificar descontos reais nas lojas físicas.
articles.summary: A Black Friday movimenta o comércio com consumidores em busca de promoções em Teresina; ferramentas ajudam a identificar descontos reais nas lojas físicas.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Lojas em Teresina registram movimentação intensa nesta sexta-feira (27) por causa da Black Friday , data marcada por promoções e descontos no comércio. Entre os consumidores que aproveitaram as ofertas está a dona de casa Sandra Torres, que percorreu cerca de 40 quilômetros para comprar uma bicicleta para o filho .

Para Sandra, o dia começou cedo: às 4h30, ela já estava de pé. À TV Clube , a dona de casa, que mora em Altos , no Norte do Piauí, caracterizou a Black Friday como a data mais aguardada do ano para fazer compras em um preço mais acessível.

"Eu sai 4h30 de casa, peguei o primeiro carro e já estou aqui antes da loja abrir", afirmou.

Outra estratégia foi adotada pela mãe do estudante Luiz Felipe. Enquanto ela escolhia as roupas que pretendia comprar, o jovem aguardava na fila do caixa.

"Ela veio para cá e não quis entrar em fila nenhuma, eu que to pegando tudo. Muita espera", brincou.

Gerente de uma loja de roupas femininas, Marcelo Paz afirmou que a quantidade de compradores superou as expectativas .

"Não estávamos esperando algo tão grande, está sendo muito maior do que esperávamos", comentou.

Mulher viaja mais de 40 km para comprar bicicleta em promoção da Black Friday no PI — Foto: Reprodução/Tv Clube

Um painel interativo foi disponibilizado pela Superintendência de Defesa e Proteção do Consumidor (Sudecon), vinculada à Secretaria de Segurança Pública do Piauí (SSP-PI). Nele, é possível comparar preços de produtos em até três lojas. Confira aqui .

A plataforma também apresenta quatro orientações para os consumidores antes de finalizar as compras, como registrar os preços por meio de fotos das etiquetas ou capturas de tela dos anúncios, além de comparar valores em diferentes lojas e sites.

Os consumidores também são orientados a verificar as formas de pagamento, os prazos e as regras para troca dos produtos.

"Promessa de vendedor só vale como prova se estiver na nota, no pedido ou em mensagem guardada", informa o site.

O Ministério Público do Estado do Piauí (MPPI), por meio do Programa de Proteção e Defesa do Consumidor (Procon), também disponibilizou um painel que ajuda a identificar falsas promoções e possíveis aumentos injustificados nos preços dos produtos. Confira aqui .

O levantamento reúne os preços de 150 produtos distribuídos em 15 categorias e pesquisados em 13 lojas físicas de Teresina.

Nas duas plataformas, os consumidores também podem registrar denúncias e reclamações.

articles.title: Homem é preso em flagrante após furtar peças de bronze de cemitério  | G1
articles.standfirst: Suspeito de 49 anos foi detido depois de ser flagrado no local fora do horário de funcionamento; material recuperado é avaliado em mais de R$ 3 mil.
articles.summary: Um homem de 49 anos foi preso em flagrante após furtar dezenas de peças de bronze de túmulos de um cemitério. O suspeito foi detido por agentes da Guarda Civil.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Um homem de 49 anos foi preso em flagrante na quinta-feira (26) após furtar dezenas de peças de bronze de túmulos de um cemitério. O suspeito foi detido por agentes da Guarda Civil após tentar fugir do local.

O crime foi descoberto depois que uma testemunha viu o homem dentro do cemitério em um horário em que o espaço já estava fechado ao público e acionou a corporação. Ao notar a chegada dos guardas, o suspeito tentou escapar, mas foi alcançado, abordado e acabou confessando o furto.

Com ele, os agentes apreenderam dezenas de objetos de bronze, avaliados em pouco mais de R$ 3 mil.

O diretor do cemitério compareceu ao local e confirmou que as peças haviam sido arrancadas das sepulturas. Segundo ele, o espaço já havia sido alvo de furtos semelhantes anteriormente.

O suspeito foi encaminhado à delegacia e permanece à disposição da Justiça.

articles.title: Câmara de Campinas cancela sessão para votar reforma da Previdência | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão ocorreu mesmo após a Justiça autorizar o uso de força mínima para retirar os manifestantes que ocupam as entradas da Casa Legislativa desde as 7h.
articles.summary: Decisão ocorreu mesmo após a Justiça autorizar o uso de força mínima para retirar os manifestantes que ocupam as entradas da Casa Legislativa desde as 7h.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

A Câmara de Vereadores de Campinas cancelou a sessão extraordinária que havia sido convocada para esta sexta-feira (27) para votar o projeto de reforma da Previdência .

A decisão ocorreu mesmo após a Justiça autorizar o uso de força mínima para retirar os manifestantes que ocupam as entradas da Casa Legislativa desde as 7h.

Segundo a assessoria da Câmara, a presidência optou por não fazer uso da força para retirar os manifestantes, e também não fará, nesta sexta-feira, a reunião de forma remota, como havia sido autorizada pelo judiciário.

O cancelamento ocorreu cerca de 1 hora após o oficial de Justiça comparecer ao local para notificar a decisão da 1ª Vara da Fazenda Pública de Campinas, assinada pelo juiz Mauro Iuji Fukumoto, que autorizou a Casa e a Guarda Municipal usarem "força mínima" para desobstruir as entradas do Legislativo .

"Em que pese o status constitucional da liberdade de manifestação, não pode tal direito ser utilizado com a finalidade de impedir o exercício da atividade legislativa, como se alega a estar ocorrendo. É perfeitamente lícito que os manifestantes permaneçam em torno da Câmara Municipal, mas não podem impedir o acesso dos vereadores, servidores da Câmara e profissionais da imprensa", escreveu Fukumoto.

Trabalhadores durante manifestação contra a reforma da Previdência dos servidores de Campinas (SP) — Foto: Johnny Inselsperger/EPTV

O projeto propõe a alteração da idade mínima para aposentadoria das mulheres de 55 anos para 60 anos. Para homens, a ampliação é de 62 anos para 65 anos. Além disso, serão exigidos 25 anos de contribuição, 10 anos de serviço público e 5 anos no cargo.

A proposta, defendida pela prefeitura como necessária para adequar as regras locais à reforma da Previdência aprovada pelo Congresso Nacional em 2019 e para enfrentar uma dívida de R$ 13 bilhões no Instituto de Previdência Social do Município de Campinas (Camprev), afeta os planos de servidores.

Um exemplo é o educador de arte Hilton Aparecido da Silva, que atua no serviço público desde 1998 e vinha se planejamento para aposentar em janeiro de 2029. Se a mudança for aprovada, ele terá de seguir na ativa até abril de 2032.

"O mais injusto é que você faz um planejamento da vida inteira e de repente vê isso se quebrar", afirma o educador de arte.

A principal alteração está na idade exigida para servidores .

Como é hoje Mulheres: 55 anos Homens: 60 anos

Como ficaria Mulheres: 62 anos Homens: 65 anos

Além da idade mínima, serão exigidos 25 anos de contribuição, 10 anos de serviço público e 5 anos no cargo .

➡ Na prática, mulheres poderão ter que trabalhar até 7 anos a mais e homens poderão ter que trabalhar até 5 anos a mais. A alíquota de contribuição permanece em 14%, segundo a proposta.

Professores, pessoas com deficiência e eletivos à aposentadoria especial estão sujeitos a outras regras — confira nesta reportagem .

Quem já tiver cumprido todos os requisitos para aposentadoria antes da publicação da nova lei poderá se aposentar pelas regras atuais. A proteção também vale para aposentados, pensionistas e servidores que já tenham adquirido esse direito.

Para quem ainda não completou os requisitos para se aposentar, o projeto cria duas regras de transição: sistema de pontos e pedágio de 100% .

Regras de Transição da Previdência de Campinas - PLC 87/2026

Prefeitura de Campinas negocia termos da reforma previdenciária com sindicatos — Foto: Carlos Bassan/Prefeitura de Campinas

Embora o debate não tenha oficialmente começado, o texto original já deverá sofrer mudanças, com emendas apresentadas pelo vereador e líder do governo na Casa, Paulo Haddad (PSD).

Isso porque uma negociação entre sindicatos e o Executivo, nesta quinta (26), selou quatro alterações no projeto — entenda abaixo.

Entre as principais mudanças estão o aumento dos requisitos para acesso ao benefício, a adoção de novas regras de transição e alterações na forma de cálculo dos proventos. A proposta poderá afetar cerca de 15 mil servidores na ativa.

A administração municipal afirma que a mudança é necessária para adequar as regras locais à reforma da Previdência aprovada pelo governo federal em 2019 e para enfrentar um déficit atuarial estimado em R$ 13 bilhões no Instituto de Previdência Social do Município de Campinas (Camprev).

O município precisa aprovar as mudanças até dezembro para cumprir exigências ligadas ao parcelamento de uma dívida superior a R$ 330 milhões com o instituto previdenciário. Caso contrário, o acordo pode ser suspenso.

Desde que foi protocolada na Câmara, a proposta tem sido alvo de críticas de servidores. Um dos principais impactos apontados está na perda da integralidade e da paridade para parte dos trabalhadores, o que pode reduzir o valor recebido após a aposentadoria e exigir mais tempo de permanência na ativa.

A repercussão negativa a Prefeitura negociasse termos, nesta quinta, com o Sindicato dos Trabalhadores do Serviço Público Municipal de Campinas (STMC) e o Sindicato dos Funcionários do Poder Legislativo de Campinas (SinFPol).

Quatro mudanças no projeto original foram acertadas:

Garantia de paridade e integralidade para o servidor que ingressou no serviço público até 2003 e que optar pela transição pela soma de pontos independentemente de idade mínima;

Garantia de que o reajuste de ativos e inativos será o mesmo;

Atualização dos aportes previstos em valor nominal pela inflação;

Presunção de dependência econômica até três pisos municipais para obtenção da pensão por morte.

Essas alterações deverão ser apresentadas como emendas por Haddad, líder do governo na Câmara, antes da sessão extraordinária desta sexta.

"Os avanços são resultado de um processo de discussão e negociação do STMC e dos Conselheiros do Camprev. (...) O STMC seguirá atuando nas negociações e defendendo a incorporação de novas mudanças ao texto antes da votação definitiva, especialmente no que diz respeito às regras de transição e ao tempo adicional de contribuição exigido dos servidores", declarou o STMC.

Já o presidente do SinFPol, Fábio Dias, destacou que as negociações deverão continuar na semana que vem, antes da votação em definitivo do projeto. Ele disse que o sindicato está longe de estar satisfeito .

"Os pontos que foram negociados estamos de acordo, sem dúvida. Foi uma luta muito difícil, são pontos muito importantes, que nós conseguimos chegar a um consenso com o governo, mas existem outros indispensáveis", afirmou Dias.

O representante do SinFPol citou dois exemplos de insatisfação: o primeiro é a mudança no cálculo do valor da aposentadoria. Atualmente, é feita uma média dos 80% maiores salários em carteira — os outros 20% são desconsiderados. A reforma prevê considerar 100% .

"Isso joga o cálculo da aposentadoria muito para baixo, né? Abaixa muito a aposentadoria das pessoas. Isso é um ponto que não podemos abrir mão, em nenhuma hipótese. Cogita-se greve no município, se nós não conseguirmos chegar a um acordo quanto a isso", disparou.

E o segundo exemplo são as regras de transição . Os sindicatos têm tentado alterar as regras de pontos e de pedágio. "É uma negociação difícil também", reconheceu.

Base negocia; oposição não abre mão de derrubada

Servidores públicos durante manifestação em frente a Câmara Municipal de Campinas — Foto: Johnny Inselsperger/EPTV

O lema para a base do prefeito tem sido que o projeto "não se trata de ser popular, mas de ser necessário", segundo Haddad. É por isso que a impopularidade não tem afetado, até o momento, a votação do texto. O caminho adotado é o da negociação .

O líder do governo ficará responsável por apresentar emendas conforme as alterações forem acordadas. A expectativa dele é de aprovar a propositura. "Em relação às manifestações dos servidores, elas são sempre bem-vindas. É a Casa do Povo e eles têm todo direito de se manifestar", declarou.

"Vale lembrar que, quando ocorreu a reforma da Previdência em 2019, foi permitido que para servidores federais, estaduais e municipais fossem realizadas reformas específicas, desde que em moldes similares. É isso que está ocorrendo agora e o próprio Ministério da Previdência exige que seja feito até dezembro para que Campinas não perca o Certificado de Regularidade Previdenciário", defendeu Haddad.

O vereador lembrou que a ausência do certificado proibiria o município de realizar transferências voluntárias da União e a celebração de convênios, contratos, acordos e ajustes com órgãos federais. Também ficam vedados empréstimos, financiamentos, avais e subvenções, inclusive por instituições financeiras federais.

Por outro lado, a oposição não vê outro caminho senão tentar a derrubada da reforma . Segundo a vereadora Fernanda Souto (Psol), o erro da proposta já começou no horário da primeira votação (às 9h desta sexta), que dificultaria a presença de trabalhadores.

"Apesar do prefeito trabalhar para atropelar as discussões sobre o projeto e impor a votação em uma sessão extraordinária, acredito que teremos muitos servidores acompanhando a votação", comentou.

A parlamentar disse que não houve qualquer discussão com os servidores antes do texto ser protocolado na Casa. Além disso, Souto apontou que a solução para os problemas financeiros do Camprev não pode passar pela retirada de direitos dos servidores .

"A Prefeitura precisa fazer um plano de amortização da dívida com o Camprev e isso é possível. A cidade tem acumulado aumento de receitas correntes ano a ano, acima da inflação e tem condições de honrar com essa responsabilidade", explicou.

Questionada sobre a possibilidade de negociar termos do projeto, a vereadora foi taxativa. "Nesse momento, não há nenhuma discussão nesse sentido. Exigimos a retirada do projeto", finalizou.

Nesta quinta, trabalhadores encaminharam mensagens por meio de redes sociais convocando para uma mobilização na Câmara . A orientação é que, nos locais de trabalho, os servidores conversem com as respectivas coordenações para que seja possível manter 30% do efetivo.

"Precisamos chegar cedo, nos organizar e comparecer em peso! O momento exige união, responsabilidade e mobilização. E não se esqueçam: essa luta não é contra coordenadores, chefias ou colegas. É uma luta pelos direitos de toda a categoria", trouxe o informe.

No entanto, a Prefeitura de Campinas informou, em nota, que as faltas sem justificativa serão registradas na frequência funcional .

"As regras de frequência devem ser mantidas. Em caso de afastamento por motivo de saúde, é necessário apresentar atestado médico. O uso de abonos depende de autorização prévia da chefia imediata. Também devem ser observadas as demais hipóteses de afastamento previstas em lei."

articles.title: Marital rape: Millions of wives in South Asia unprotected - study
articles.summary: More than 100 countries have outlawed marital rape, but a large part of South Asia has not.
articles.body:
Failure to fully criminalise marital rape leaves millions of women and girls unprotected in eight South Asian countries, where intimate partner violence is 35% higher than the global average, says a new study.

More than 100 countries have outlawed marital rape, but a large part of South Asia - India, Afghanistan, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh - remain among the three dozen countries which haven't.

The only South Asian country where rape within marriage attracts the same penalty as any other rape is The Maldives.

Nepal and Bhutan have criminalised marital rape, but apply lesser penalties, says the study by Samaj, a coalition of women's rights groups in the region.

South Asia's marital rape laws largely stem from British colonial rule, says Ranjeeta Silwal of Equality Now, a global women's rights group part of Samaj.

The law, dating to 1860 in India and Bangladesh and 1885 in Sri Lanka, lists exceptions to rape - including sex by a man with his adult wife.

Campaigners say the law is outdated and forced sex is rape, regardless of the perpetrator. Experts warn marital sexual violence harms women's physical, psychological, emotional and sexual well-being.

More than 100 countries have criminalised marital rape, including the UK, which changed its law in 1991. But the exemption remains in India, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh.

Pakistan removed the marital rape exception in 2006, but no higher court has confirmed that rape laws apply within marriage. A recent high court ruling, meanwhile, granted husbands broad immunity for non-consensual sex.

Since returning to power in 2021, the Taliban have steadily dismantled women's protections in Afghanistan.

A new penal code introduced in January made matters worse, Silwal says. Under it, a husband can be prosecuted for violence against his wife only if he causes a broken bone, open wound or severe bruising. Even then, he faces just 15 days in prison if convicted.

Unsurprisingly, the code makes no mention of marital rape. But its narrow definition of punishable violence effectively denies women protection against it.

"The idea comes from the belief that consent for sex is implied in marriage, that marriage is a threshold where consent ends," Silwal told the BBC.

"But it shows a lack of awareness, it shows we are still treating women as property, that we are still very patriarchal."

The report comes amid renewed debate over marital rape across the region.

In India, 10 petitions challenging the law are pending before the Supreme Court, which is due to begin final hearings on 9 December.

Courts have delivered contradictory rulings over the years, with some judges acknowledging the law's archaic nature and urging parliament to criminalise marital rape.

There was outrage last year when a court let go a man whose wife had died after he brutally raped her.

But the Indian government, religious organisations and men's rights activists have opposed petitions in the top court, saying criminalisation of marital rape would be " excessively harsh ".

Rights groups in Bangladesh have also challenged the marital rape exception, arguing it violates constitutional rights to life, liberty and protection from torture and cruel treatment, the report says.

"Those who oppose criminalising marital rape say it would undermine the family unit and break them apart. And family is very important in our countries," Silwal says.

"They say it will affect our religious and cultural values and worry that there would be false accusations against men."

Also a change in law, she says, may not necessarily mean justice for survivors.

Silwal points to Bhutan where marital rape is a criminal offence but it's treated as a petty misdemeanour and is punishable by one month to one year.

In Nepal, the punishment for rape is between six and 20 years, but it's only up to five years for a husband who rapes his wife.

articles.title: The world’s biggest city museum opens with a $570M price tag, royal relics and a revolting ‘fatberg’
articles.summary: The new London Museum aims to be a major cultural destination where nearby clubbers might come for the 24 hour cafe, and stay to see the collection.
articles.body: Large illuminated letters spell out “London” over one of the entrances to the converted meat market in the city’s Smithfield district. It signposts the brand new London Museum, the biggest city museum in the world, which took ten years and an astounding £437 million ($570 million) to complete. Had the brains behind this epic cultural project considered adding a sub-heading, they might have quoted the city’s most celebrated literary son: Charles Dickens. “It was the best of times, it was the worst of times,” wrote Dickens in the famous opening to “A Tale of Two Cities.” Although the 1859 novel is set in London and Paris in the late 18th century, the sentiment might just as easily apply exclusively to London as depicted by this new museum and its eclectic collection of artifacts. Far from being a straight forward love letter to London, the museum sets out to tell the city’s story “in all its grit and glitter,” as declared on its website ahead of the grand opening this weekend. Celebrating its 50th anniversary this year, the institution has gained a new name as well as a new home –– from the Museum of London, to London Museum. This is more than a simple rebrand. As museums fight to stay relevant in an age where just about any artifact can be viewed online, the aim here is clearly to become a cultural destination with broad appeal. Sharon Ament, director of the museum, said she hopes the new name is a “match” with the British Museum, which saw more than 6 million visitors last year. Drawing in that kind of crowd is what Ament and her colleagues aspire to. Achieving that involves stretching the definition of museum to the max. There will be a 24-hour cafe on select days, alongside a restaurant and cocktail bar, all accessible from the street and operating outside of museum hours. There are plans to host house parties, dinner clubs and rotating displays, the first of which charts the city’s vibrant food culture. The hope, presumably, is that those who might not otherwise visit, could come in for a cappuccino or a Bloody Mary and stay –– or return –– to see Queen Victoria’s black mourning dress, Charles I’s stained execution vest or even the leather chair where Dickens is believed to have penned his masterpieces. The complex project –– which by some estimates soared at least £100 million ($131 million) over budget –– has seen the city’s General Market, which first opened in 1883, returned to public use for the first time in more than three decades. It operated for more than a century but closed during the 1990s, then falling into disrepair. A team of architects made up of Stanton Williams, Asif Khan and conservation architects Julian Harrap led the 21st century transformation which involved the expertise of more than 70 different trades, including stonemasons, blacksmiths and coppersmiths. The location alone is enough to showcase the contrast of life in the British capital. Smithfield has a bloody past, and even now, there is the ever so slight whiff of meat from the small parts of the market still in operation. But the site’s gruesome past extends beyond the meat market: It was the scene of many public executions, including that of Scottish hero William Wallace in 1305, while more than 100 people were killed when a Nazi V2 bomb fell here in 1945. A few minutes walk away, however, lies Hatton Garden, London’s historic center for diamonds and jewelry. Inside the museum that contrast is very much in evidence too, from the light and airy layout of the venue’s ground floor, to the dark underbelly of its vaults. “That grit and that juxtaposition of the joy is the wonderfulness and the hard stuff of London,” said Ament. London is one of the world’s financial powerhouses, but like many global cities it has a multi-layered past –– and present. “We need to hold that, we can’t shy away from it,” said Ament. “It’s our lives, our histories.” Likewise, Paul Williams, of Stanton Williams, said at the press preview that he hopes “this sort of duality” will “trigger the imagination” of visitors. “The transition between light and dark is so fundamental to the experience,” he said. The museum’s converted Poultry Market will open in 2028, housing temporary exhibition spaces, a dedicated learning centre and collections store. “The two buildings working together, they’re quite different,” said Williams. “One you go down to Roman level … so you’re going down into the belly of the earth. This one, the Poultry market, you’re going up to the heavens.” Objects of desire and disgust The layout of the permanent display is unconventional, following a rough –– but not steadfast –– timeline. Some is organized thematically in sections with titles such as “London as lesson” and “London as prayer.” Traditional introductory explanations have been ditched in favor of interpretations by writers and poets, a somewhat baffling decision that Ament staunchly defends. “Artists, and I include poets and writers, can sum up big ideas in really evocative ways, better than a museum interpretation person can,” she said. “They couldn’t make things up, but they used the facts as their inspiration.” Some of the items appear to have been placed in direct contrast to each other, further highlighting the rough and smooth of London life. Memorabilia from the London 2012 Olympics –– including the Olympic torch and a pair of swimming trunks in which teenage diver Tom Daley shot to fame –– sit footsteps away from a piece of twisted debris from a 1970s IRA bomb attack and headlines reporting how terrorists brought carnage to London on July 7, 2005. Continuing to push traditional boundaries, the current site is divided into three sections: Real Time, Our Time and Past Time. Visitors enter through Real Time, a former street now covered and converted into the site’s main entrance. Highlights here include street artist Banksy’s “Piranhas” sentry box, a clock tower featuring the final bell cast at the Whitechapel Bell Foundry (which also made the bell for Big Ben) and a display wall featuring live data on everything from the city’s bee population to Londoners’ listening habits. Elsewhere, the former trading floor of the General Market is taken up with Our Time, dedicated to London in living memory. The sparsely positioned displays once again highlight the city’s privilege and hardship: from the Lord Mayor’s golden state coach and a Buckingham Palace telephone switchboard with lines to the Prime Minister, to a display memorializing those who perished in the 2017 Grenfell Tower fire. Past Time, the museum’s cavernous permanent gallery, is set at Roman street level. Here visitors will meet everyone from the capital’s first prehistoric inhabitants to today’s immigrant communities. The collection features regular reminders of subterranean London. Stealing the show is the Cheapside Hoard, a dazzling collection of almost 500 pieces of 16th and 17th century jewelry which mysteriously lay buried underground until workmen unearthed it in 1912. On the grittier side, is a chunk of the Whitechapel ‘fatberg’, a 130-ton mass of oil and wet wipes found to be blocking sewers beneath east London in 2017. “The basement vaults are a space double the size of the one above ground –– one of London’s biggest hidden gems,” said Asif Khan at the press conference. He said that the addition of the Poultry Market, which was not in the original brief, had “freed this building to be more of an experiment in what the future of a museum can be.” While the aim of the project was to create something bold and exciting, Khan said it was important to “peel back enough layers of the building to reveal its own history.” Nowhere is that perhaps more literally realized than in the striking large glass window onto the railway line that cuts through the site. The sound of trains thundering past can be heard throughout the museum, but here visitors can sit, observe and reflect on the transport network powering London. “I think it’s our rumbling heart,” said Williams, who added that he and the rest of the team of architects knew early on that “this space had the capacity to suspend disbelief.” “I think even now, the people we’ve seen with their telephones, they cannot not photograph it,” he told the press conference. “Through the glass window, you don’t see the train, you just see the windows. It’s a wonderful abstract art piece that goes past. It’s mesmerizing.” Begone the museum of old It feels a world away from the former museum, which opened in 1976 on a walkway above street level which is linked to the Barbican art center. “Nobody passed by the old Museum of London,” said Ament. “People fought their way to the museum, and so here you go to a place which has got multiple entrances connected to the street and is on a transport hub.” What mattered most was making the new site “porous,” she said. “Every road we sit on is a great vibrant place in its own right. People will literally be able to just flow through. I want to open up culture and history to as many people as possible.” Ament added: “We’re about to present to the world this new, more flexible, more dynamic, more permeable way of engaging with history and with culture on your terms.”

articles.title: South Korea sends rescued fishermen back to North
articles.summary: Pyongyang has not commented on a seventh fisherman who chose to remain in the South.
articles.body:
South Korea has repatriated six of the seven North Korean fishermen it rescued from their drifting boat earlier this month.

The six fishermen crossed the maritime border between the rival states off the Korean Peninsula’s east coast on board their vessel early on Friday. They were met by a waiting North Korean ship.

On November 3, the South Korean military and coastguard authorities had rescued and towed the fishing boat after it drifted into international waters near the country’s Ulleung island.

South Korea has confirmed that the six men sent to the North had expressed a wish to return. A seventh fisherman chose to defect, according to the Unification Ministry.

Seoul added that it had notified Pyongyang of the plan through the multilateral United Nations Command, and also sent updates on Friday over an international maritime communications network.

North Korea has not commented on the fisherman who chose to remain, but the waiting vessel suggested that Pyongyang had received all communications.

North Korea severed direct communications with the South in 2024. Border tensions have escalated between the two this year.

South Korea considers North Koreans as its citizens and offers protection to defectors or repatriates those who wish to return.

Pyongyang usually takes defections seriously and has accused the South of enticing its citizens to the other side, a charge that Seoul denies.

Some 31,500 North Koreans were registered as living in the South by June, according to Unification Ministry data.

articles.title: An Australian family rejected an insurer's A$1,000 goodwill offer as their storm-damaged home deteriorated; Hollard eventually paid A$1.55 million and a court later imposed a separate A$2 million penalty
articles.summary: An Australian family received A$1.55 million from its insurer after a lengthy dispute over a storm-damaged home.
articles.body: An Australian family received A$1.55 million from its insurer after a lengthy dispute over a storm-damaged home. The family had earlier rejected a goodwill offer of just A$1,000 as the property continued to deteriorate. The insurer, Hollard Insurance Partners Limited, has now been ordered to pay a separate A$2 million penalty by the Federal Court.The case involved a family in regional Victoria whose home was damaged by a storm in October 2021. According to the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC), the insurer initially accepted the claim for roof damage but changed its decision 15 months later. By then, the house had suffered extensive damage from moisture, mould and decay.The family was left dealing with the worsening condition of its home while waiting for the insurer to resolve the claim. The property eventually became uninhabitable and was declared a total loss. Hollard took more than three years from the date of the original claim to complete the payments to the family.The Federal Court's penalty followed legal action brought by ASIC in April 2025. Hollard admitted that its handling of the claim involved serious delays, poor communication and periods of inaction. The A$2 million penalty is separate from the A$1.55 million paid to the family.Family turned down A$1,000 offerThe dispute continued even after Hollard rejected the claim. In late 2022, the family approached the insurer with a complaint about how its case had been handled. Hollard offered A$1,000 as a goodwill payment to settle the matter.The family refused the offer and approached the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA). Hollard eventually paid A$1.55 million, including an amount reflecting the total loss of the house.However, the resolution came after years of waiting. The insurer had identified the need for a structural engineering assessment during its first inspection, but the assessment was not carried out until August 2022. Its final decision on the claim came only in April 2023.The delays also affected arrangements for temporary accommodation. During this period, the family's house continued to deteriorate, with mould and moisture damage making the property increasingly difficult to live in.Judge questions insurer's handling of claimThe Federal Court criticised the way Hollard dealt with the family. Justice Button said the prolonged dispute had put the family through a stressful experience while they watched their home deteriorate.The judge also questioned why the insurer had taken around eight months to arrange an engineering assessment after the need for one was identified. He said the slow handling of the claim and the spread of mould could not simply be blamed on staff being busy or communication problems with suppliers.The court said insurers must deal with customers fairly, particularly when claims involve homes that represent a major financial asset for families. Hollard's actions in this case fell short of the standard expected of an insurer.ASIC Chair Sarah Court said the ruling should remind insurance companies that delays can have serious consequences for policyholders.She said people often approach insurers during difficult periods and should not have to face further uncertainty because their claims are not handled properly.Regulator steps up scrutiny of insurersASIC has previously raised concerns about delays and weaknesses in the way insurers communicate with policyholders.In a separate report published by ABC News on November 26, ASIC was reported to have initiated legal action against another major insurer, AIG Australia. The regulator alleged that AIG failed to respond to or notify customers about delays in 534 insurance complaints within the required 30-day period.Some customers reportedly waited several months for decisions. The complaints involved people who were unwell, injured or had recently lost family members. ASIC also alleged that AIG's systems failed to properly track complaints and alert staff when responses were due. The regulator is seeking penalties and other orders against AIG.You use AI every day. articles.title: Bristol Hippodrome to close for major refurbishment
articles.summary: Bristol Hippodrome will be shut from January while it undergoes upgrades and repairs.
articles.body:
A city centre theatre is to close for seven months to allow for a major revamp.

Designed to protect its long-term future, the Bristol Hippodrome will shut its doors for the improvements from 4 January to 2 August 2027.

The refurbishment will include repairs to the theatre's historic structure and roof, as well as upgrades to essential heating, fire detection, cooling and water systems.

Theatre director Ben Phillips said: "This work is all about looking after our theatre and ensuring it remains a thriving home for live entertainment for future generations."

"While we'll miss welcoming audiences during the closure period, these improvements will help secure the long-term future of this much-loved venue and allow us to continue creating unforgettable experiences for years to come," Phillips added.

Visitors and performers will also benefit from refurbished public and backstage toilet facilities, the theatre said.

The theatre, which has a capacity 1,951, first opened in 1912.

The Grade II listed building was designed by renowned theatre architect Frank Matcham for Sir Oswald Stoll, who also owned the London Coliseum and founded the Royal Variety Performance.

The final performance on 3 January will be the Sleeping Beauty panto featuring Strictly Come Dancing's Craig Revel Horwood and BBC Radio Bristol presenter Joe Sims.

Multiple shows, including Grease, The Comedy About Spied and Pretty Woman, are already scheduled for the reopening in August.

Further details about the project, including timings and reopening plans, will be announced soon, the theatre added.

articles.title: Revolutionary War’s ‘Captain Molly’ took up her husband’s fight for freedom
articles.summary: Margaret Corbin took her fallen husband's place at a cannon as 8,000 British and Hessian troops stormed Fort Washington, earning fame as "Captain Molly."
articles.body: The fall of Fort Washington in Manhattan in November 1776 was one of the lowest points in the war for Gen. George Washington. Multiple sources report seeing the general cry like a child while watching the action through his spyglass from across the river in New Jersey. That led to over 2,800 American troops being taken prisoner, in addition to the strategic loss of the fort and huge battle casualties. One of those who survived the conflict, however, was one of the first female combat veterans: Margaret Corbin. At daybreak on Nov. 16, 1776, when British Gen. William Howe attacked the clifftop, earthen-walled American fortress with some 8,000 British and Hessian troops from four sides, Margaret’s husband manned a cannon as part of the 1st Company of Pennsylvania Artillery. The company, with its furious fire into the hordes of advancing Hessian troops, was supporting several companies of the crack-shot riflemen positioned outside the fort walls. Outnumbered three to one, commanding officer Col. Robert Magaw tried to hold the indefensible fort by placing these elite riflemen about a mile outside the fort, along the likely avenues of the British advance. EVERYDAY REVOLUTIONARY WAR HEROES TAKE CENTER STAGE IN TRUMP'S 'SPIRIT OF '76' EXHIBIT The full story of these remarkable riflemen and the role of the Pennsylvania long rifle in helping win the Revolutionary War can be found in my latest bestselling book, "Revolutionary Snipers: Washington’s Frontier Commandos Whose Marksmanship Forged a New Way of War and Helped Win the Revolution," the third book in a trilogy on the elite units of the war. This groundbreaking look at the Revolutionary War recounts the untold story of the Continental Army’s first soldiers in an immersive "Band of Brothers"-style narrative that puts the reader in the boots of the snipers who preceded today’s U.S. Army special operators. PATRICK K O’DONNELL: REVOLUTION’S EPIC TEST SHOWED STRENGTH OF OUR GREATEST GENERATION When a bullet felled Margaret’s husband as he manned a cannon, she sprang into action. A fiery redhead known for her foul mouth and brashness, Corbin "heroically filled the post of her husband, who was killed by her side," words Congress used when officially recognizing her status as one of America’s first female combat veterans. The intrepid woman typified the grit and independence intrinsically woven into the DNA of people of the American frontier. She had suffered the death of her father during an Indian raid and the kidnapping of her mother, whom she never saw again. She had followed her husband into war as a camp follower. Known as "Mollies," camp followers had a complicated relationship with the military. Many officers despised having these wives, mothers, daughters, mistresses and their children along, believing they distracted soldiers and slowed their movements. AMERICA HAS FOUNDING FATHERS. A CATHOLIC SAINT WAS A FOUNDING MOTHER Others noted that men might not continue fighting if they couldn’t bring their wives. Washington wrote that he "was obliged to give Provisions to the extra Women in these regiments, or lose by Desertion, perhaps to the enemy, some of the oldest and best Soldiers in the Service." Camp followers provided valuable services as well as working as laundresses, cooks or nurses. A few even spied on British camps while working as cooks or laundresses there. But as Margaret Corbin demonstrated, some did even more. THE STORY BEHIND BETSY ROSS AND THE FIRST AMERICAN FLAG AS AMERICA CELEBRATES 250TH BIRTHDAY As she stepped up to help work the gun after her husband fell, musket balls or grapeshot tore into her chest, arm and jaw, gravely wounding her. The men nicknamed the courageous widow "Captain Molly." Nearly every member of the company she served with would be injured or killed during the stand. The Americans, however, made the Hessians pay a high price as well in blood for their victory. After the battle, British surgeons found Captain Molly Corbin barely alive, stabilized her and later paroled her. Although Corbin never regained the use of her left arm and continued to suffer from her numerous combat wounds, the hard-drinking, swearing, proud, disabled combat veteran found employment at West Point in the Corps of Invalids for wounded soldiers, where she often smoked a pipe and wore an artillery coat over her dress. articles.title: Florida man sentenced to 47 months in prison for using AI to clone streamer N3on’s voice and steal $260,000 in cryptocurrency from a meme coin project
articles.summary: Florida man David Anthony Sanchez has been sentenced to 47 months in prison for using AI to clone the voice of streamer N3on and defraud a meme coin
articles.body: Florida man David Anthony Sanchez has been sentenced to 47 months in prison for using AI to clone the voice of streamer N3on and defraud a meme coin project of $260,000 in cryptocurrency. Sanchez, from Port St. Lucie and also known as “Dave the Jewler”, passed himself off as the popular online personality, persuading the project’s organisers that the streamer had agreed to back their plans. He pleaded guilty to two federal charges of money laundering and aggravated identity theft, and the court has also ordered him to pay restitution to the project’s victims on top of his prison term.AI voice cloning of N3on and fake accounts helped a Florida man steal $260,000 in cryptocurrencyAccording to the US Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Florida, court records show that Sanchez set up online accounts designed to look as though they belonged to N3on. He then used them to deal with the project’s organisers while playing two parts at once, the streamer himself and his representative.To make the story stick, he executed agreements in the streamer’s name and sent over a voice recording, generated with AI, that mimicked N3on to falsely confirm his involvement. Taken in, the victims transferred cryptocurrency to accounts Sanchez controlled. A substantial portion was later converted into US dollars through transactions designed to hide where the money came from and who owned it, and Sanchez spent it for his own benefit.Who is streamer N3on, and why this is not his first brush with AI deepfakes and digital doublesThe streamer at the centre of the case is Mikyle Rafiq, who goes by N3on online, Engadget reported. This wasn't his first encounter with a digital double. Citing Aftermath, the report said he once used a deepfake of himself to keep his Kick stream running around the clock.Acting US Attorney Yara Lorenzo Klukas used the sentencing to send a message. “Behind every fraud scheme are real people who suffer real financial harm,” she said in the office’s statement. She added that Sanchez exploited AI to manipulate unsuspecting victims' trust, and that the sentence reflects a commitment to holding to account those who use emerging technologies to defraud others.US District Judge Melissa Damian imposed the term, which was announced on 24 November, following an investigation by the FBI’s Miami field office.You use AI every day. articles.title: Grace Tame: Ex-media executive admits saying child sex abuse survivor 'looking to be raped again'
articles.summary: The former Murdoch media executive was overheard at an event referring to the way Grace Tame was dressed.
articles.body:
An Australian former media executive has admitted he said a child sex abuse survivor and prominent advocate "must be looking to be raped again" because of the way she was dressed at an event.

Grace Tame, 31, was groomed and abused by a teacher and has been honoured as Australian of the Year in 2021 for her advocacy work on child safety.

In an op-ed for independent media outlet Crikey, Tame said she overheard Matt Handbury speaking to a friend, and was left distressed by the remark and the failure of others who heard it to intervene.

Handbury, nephew of Rupert Murdoch and a former executive at his firms, has not responded to a BBC request for comment, but in an email to Tame said he regretted the "highly objectionable" comment as soon as he said it.

Tame wrote in the Crikey article that she confronted Handbury - who she hadn't met before - immediately, and again later in the evening to check she had heard him correctly.

She said the encounter at the University of New South Wales event last week triggered flashbacks to her abuse and left her feeling like she would vomit.

"My whole body was prickling in distress," she wrote for Crikey.

"The many men and women who'd seen the confrontation were incredulous, and quick to express their anger at Matt's behaviour... Ironically though, in a room full of seasoned activists, journalists, lawyers and actual whistleblowers, not one person besides me took Matt to task in the heat of the moment."

The next day, in an email seen by the BBC, Handbury, 77, apologised for the "attempt at humour in less than poor taste".

"I did make reference to your strikingly attractive get-up... I also said: 'She must be looking to be raped again.'

He thanked her for "calling me out" and "opening my eyes more fully to this flaw in my nature which I will certainly be discussing with my very non-misogynist shrink".

"But no-one can deny you looked absolutely fabulous last night," he said, before signing off.

Handbury ran Murdoch Magazines for 13 years after buying the business from his uncle in 1991. He sold it to Seven Network's subsidiary Pacific Publications in 2004.

Tame said Handbury's remarks were "especially egregious" because it referenced a "very real, criminally tested traumatic experience, which he knew about" rather than an "imagined harm".

"It swiftly reawakened deep-seated physical wounds and haunting memories. How is that funny?"

From the age of 15, Tame was groomed and raped by her 58-year-old maths teacher Nicolaas Ockert Bester. He was later found guilty and served one year and nine months in jail for sexually abusing Tame when she was his student in 2011.

"They're not always as extreme, public or evidenced, but these kinds of experiences are part of my everyday life," Tame wrote on Instagram of Handbury's remarks.

"I'm tired of the maltreatment; and the gaslighting that follows. Tired of being provoked, then asked why I'm angry.

"I'm tired of copping more flak for fighting injustice than those who mete it out."

If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support can be found at the BBC's Action Line .

articles.title: Australia sanctions suspects in Iran-linked anti-Semitic attacks
articles.summary: Sanctions aim to restrict funds for two men alleged to have planned attacks for IRGC.
articles.body:
Australia has imposed sanctions on two men accused of orchestrating anti-Semitic arson attacks on behalf of Iran.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong said in a statement on Friday that the “counterterrorism financing sanctions” targeted Zohair Hassib and Kazem Hamad.

The pair is alleged to have used a “complex ⁠chain of proxies” to attack a kosher restaurant in Sydney and the Adass Israel Synagogue in Melbourne in 2024 at the behest of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

Wong said the sanctions would restrict the pair’s access to funds that could be used to carry out attacks, by making it a criminal offence to make assets available to them.

“These sanctions are an important step in disrupting the IRGC’s ability to ⁠conduct attacks against Australians and Australian interests,” she ⁠said.

In the aftermath of the 2024 attacks , Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced the launch of a police task force on anti-Semitism .

In August 2025, Australia accused Iran of orchestrating the fires, a charge that Tehran denied. The Iranian ambassador was ordered to leave the country, while Canberra suspended operations at its Tehran embassy and ‌listed the IRGC as a “terrorist” organisation.

The Australian Security Intelligence Organisation said in its annual threat assessment in June it was investigating alleged Iran-linked agents, sharing details of their activities but withholding their ⁠names.

Spy chief Mike Burgess described them as an Australian who was “a senior agent of the IRGC Quds Force running its networks around the world,” and an Australian crime figure recruited by Iran through a web of Iraqi-based militia groups who had been arrested in Iraq in January.

“Knowing full well they were being directed ‌by ‌the Iranian regime, these individuals orchestrated two attacks on buildings associated with Jewish Australians,” Burgess said.

Friday’s statement named the men for the first time.

The sanctions listing shows Hassib was born in Australia and is a citizen of Australia and Afghanistan, and is now living in Iran.

Hamad, alleged to be behind an illicit tobacco ring in Australia, was arrested in Iraq after a joint investigation by police from both countries.

articles.title: China tests makeshift floating bridges in amphibious landing drills near Taiwan
articles.summary: China is staging a weeks-long amphibious landing drill in the province facing Taiwan, testing a new   floating bridge, satellite images and a report showed.
articles.body: China is staging a weeks-long amphibious landing drill in the province facing Taiwan, testing a new method to land troops ashore by linking civilian vessels into a makeshift floating bridge, satellite images and a research report showed. China views democratically governed Taiwan as its own territory, despite Taipei’s rejection of Beijing’s sovereignty claims, and has never renounced the use of force to bring it under Chinese control. The exercise, in Dacheng Bay in China’s southeastern province of Fujian, was first spotted on November 1, according to satellite images and a report by geospatial data company ingeniSPACE reviewed by Reuters. “The People’s Liberation Army appeared to be rehearsing low-signature methods to provide logistical support to forces that could be involved in a first island chain invasion scenario,” said Jason Wang, the company’s chief operating officer. “Using civilian ships to enable bridging of heavy equipment and materiel from deeper waters creates additional locations they can use along the Taiwan coastline.” A senior security official briefed on the drill in Dacheng Bay, just 175 miles from Taiwan’s main island, confirmed it was still in progress on Friday, but made no direct link to local elections set for the next day. Vessels maneuver around bay Analysis of the images from Nov. 1 to 16 showed the vessels maneuvered around the bay, forming and dismantling a floating bridge about 2,600 ft long, in activity also seen in images from commercial providers Vantor and Planet Labs. Eight civilian vessels participated, made up of four barges, two semi-submersible and two powered, along with four landing craft, as well as smaller support vessels and Chinese navy ships nearby, ingeniSPACE’s analysis and tracking data showed. No purpose-built bridging equipment was observed, suggesting China’s military may be honing its use of existing civilian maritime resources to improvise landing infrastructure in a combat scenario, ingeniSPACE said. The senior security official confirmed the report details. The drill was designed to “practice the swift seizure of small islands” and was “very targeted” at contingencies along the first island chain, the arc of islands stretching from Japan through Taiwan and the Philippines, the official said. It appeared to be part of this year’s “All-Military Strategic Exercise” by the Chinese military, and was routine but held later than in previous years, added the official, who sought anonymity, as the matter is a sensitive one. China’s defense ministry did not respond to a request for comment. Its training was “entirely legitimate and reasonable”, it said on Thursday, when asked about recent PLA drills in the region. Taiwan’s defense ministry said it was aware of Chinese military activity in Dacheng Bay, including the use of civilian vessels in exercises, and was weighing the implications for security in the Taiwan Strait and peace in the region. China appears to be constantly refining coastal drills, said military attaches based in Asia, reflecting the immense task of attempting an amphibious landing across waters as wide as the Taiwan Strait. Rival militaries, including that of Taiwan, are known to scrutinise such efforts, they said. The drills are being held near Dongshan Island, visited by Chinese President Xi Jinping in 2024 and the site of a famous Cold War-era victory for the PLA. Here, in 1953, China’s military fought off an attempted invasion by Republic of China forces, which had fled to Taiwan in 1949 at the end of a civil war with Mao Zedong’s communists. While China ties have not been the focus of campaigning for Taiwan’s weekend local elections, Beijing has repeatedly denounced the ruling party’s candidate for Taipei mayor, whom it calls a “separatist”. Jamming activity seen at drill location Jamming activity was observed in the area where the drill was held, ingeniSPACE’s Wang added, citing a blurry synthetic aperture radar image obtained by the company. Taiwan has previously disclosed Chinese amphibious landing drills in Dacheng Bay in 2023 and 2024 involving roll-on/roll-off freighters. Both took place in September. Reuters documented similar drills off the southern coast of Guangdong in August last year, showing China was rehearsing the use of civilian shipping to supplement any Taiwan operation. The drill showed China’s military was increasingly focused on island-group operations, added the senior security official, but cautioned against overstating its battlefield value. “There is still some distance between innovation and fantasy,” the official said, adding that barges would be “live targets” in wartime.

articles.title: Spain’s Sánchez stood up against Trump. His own voters may be about to bring him down
articles.summary: As Spaniards prepare to vote Sunday, PM Pedro Sánchez is fighting a challenge from the center-right People’s Party on issues including housing, corruption and migration.
articles.body: For much of the past few years, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has enjoyed the kind of international reputation that few politicians do. A staunch supporter of Ukraine and vocal advocate for Palestinian rights, Sánchez, 54, has positioned himself as a moral compass for progressives in Europe. And while some European leaders compromised and sought to curry favor with US President Donald Trump in his second term, Sánchez chose defiance. “We don’t want anything to do with Spain,” Trump said on March 3, after Madrid denied Washington use of its jointly operated bases for direct strikes on Iran, one of many disagreements between the two NATO allies. The Spanish leader also rejected the White House’s demand that members of the alliance increase defense spending to 5% of GDP, prompting further criticism. The attacks burnished Sánchez’s status in Europe as the torchbearer for a new strategy for dealing with Trump. But at home, the view has, for some time, been strikingly different on a broader range of matters. After eight years in power, the corruption scandals embroiling those around him, the migrant disaster in the Spanish exclave of Ceuta, two catastrophic train crashes, a housing affordability crisis and, last but not least, an economy that though booming on paper continues not to deliver for ordinary people, the fatigue among Spaniards is palpable. The last few months of his premiership have been plagued by successive strikes involving teachers, medical staff, rail workers and others, who say their living standards have been in decline. It was the failure to pass emergency measures to curb the housing crisis that finally brought down Sánchez’s coalition, prompting him to call a snap election last month. As voters prepare to cast their ballots on Sunday, most opinion polls have Sánchez and his center-left Spanish Socialist Workers’ Party (PSOE) trailing behind the center-right People’s Party (PP). A charismatic and clever operator on the campaign trail, with a history as a political survivor who has consistently defied the odds, Sánchez has been able to reduce the gap between his party and PP in recent weeks. Yet, even if he finishes ahead, most polls suggest it is highly unlikely PSOE and the other parties on the left will be able to secure enough votes to prevent a right-wing majority and a widely anticipated governing coalition between PP and the far-right Vox party. If this happens, it’ll be the first time since the death of dictator Francisco Franco in 1975 and the instalment of a democratic system that the far right has been part of a Spanish government. ‘Persistent negligence’ PP’s Alberto Núñez Feijóo – Sánchez’s main opponent – has run on a platform to right what he sees as the wrongs of the past eight years. His campaign ads and billboards across Spain read “the necessary change,” or “the necessary president.” In effect, Feijóo, 65, is selling competence and rigor, in contrast to the chaos and spectacle he says has been the defining trait of the PSOE over the past few years: that is, something Spaniards may not necessarily desire but actually need. “I’m not running to entertain Spain,” he said during an interview with Spanish newspaper La Razón on November 4. “I’m running to serve Spain.” PP has taken aim at many of the crises they say have been the hallmark of PSOE’s rule. Chief among them are the two high-speed rail crashes this year, which killed 115 people and injured more than 300 others in total. “You have managed the high-speed rail network with persistent negligence,” Feijóo told Sánchez during a head-to-head televised debate last week, accusing the Spanish prime minister and his government of not taking action despite repeated warnings and safety failures. Sánchez has promised to investigate and address problems. Feijóo and the PP have criticized PSOE’s handling of and lack of accountability for an April 2025 blackout that left Spain without electricity for nearly 16 hours. They’ve also attacked what Feijóo calls an open-door policy on migration, blaming it for an increase in migrant boat crossings that has overwhelmed public services in Spain’s Canary Islands, off northwest Africa, as well as the deadly surge of migrants into Ceuta in July. Vox, led by Santiago Abascal, has put migration front and center of its campaign, defending what it calls a “remigration” policy for irregular immigrants while blaming them for a rise in crime and accusing them of draining resources meant for Spaniards. Neither of those claims is supported by official Spanish data, but Vox’s message has resonated, putting the radical party in prime position to potentially join a governing coalition after November 29. Corruption erodes trust When Sánchez became prime minister in 2018, he did so after unseating former PP leader Mariano Rajoy, whose government was engulfed by a series of corruption scandals. As he called for a vote of no confidence in Rajoy’s government in parliament, Sánchez said the country needed a “democratic regeneration,” one that would restore people’s faith in the country’s institutions. But since assuming the premiership, his own inner circle has been plagued by allegations of graft. In June, his former transport minister and right-hand man José Luis Ábalos was sentenced to 24 years in prison, convicted on corruption charges and accused of taking kickbacks from the purchase of facemasks during the Covid-19 pandemic. The previous month, the PSOE headquarters in Madrid was raided by police as authorities investigated several of Sánchez’s close allies, including former Prime Minister José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero, who’s denied wrongdoing. Sánchez’s wife, Begoña Gómez, has also been ordered to stand trial over alleged influence peddling and misappropriation of public funds, charges she denies. His brother, David, was convicted in July of administrative misconduct but cleared of influence peddling. Sánchez said he “never knew” of his former minister’s practices and vowed the government’s full cooperation, adding there can be no “room for impunity.” At the same time, he’s portrayed accusations against his wife as politically motivated persecution. In an interview with CNN’s Chief International Anchor Christiane Amanpour in September, he argued he and his government had been “very tough” on corruption but claimed “other cases” were “maneuvers from the opposition” to try to force him out. Sánchez has never been named in any of the corruption scandals and has consistently denied any wrongdoing. Yet Spain’s far right has been able to paint a different picture, on this and other issues, through messaging heavily amplified on social media The initial investigation into Sanchez’s wife originated from a legal complaint – based on media reports, some of which later turned out to be false – by a small civil servants’ union called Manos Limpias, or Clean Hands, which has ties to the far right. Vox later applied to join the proceedings through a Spanish legal mechanism that allows third parties to participate in criminal prosecutions. Spanish courts have allowed the key allegations to proceed but this example illustrates how Vox and others on Spain’s political fringes have been able to transform these controversies into a broader indictment of Sánchez and his government. Cost-of-living pressures Sánchez has repeatedly reminded Spanish voters he’s presided over a period of rapid and sustained economic growth. Over the past few years, Spain’s economy has been one of the fastest growing in Europe, outpacing the likes of Germany, France, Italy or the United Kingdom, and the economic argument is usually a strong one: Decades of research show voters tend to reward incumbents with a strong performance on the economy. Since 2018, Spain has seen overall unemployment fall from 15% to 10%, and youth unemployment shrink from 34% to 22%. The monthly minimum wage has also risen from €735 ($806) to €1,221 ($1,230), a 66% increase. But the cost of living has also increased. The median wage has risen at a much slower pace than the minimum and, after inflation, the average worker’s purchasing power has remained largely unchanged. Critics also argue the government has failed to capitalize on the economic boom to improve public services and people’s access to affordable housing. Rents across Spain are now 44% higher than they were when Sánchez first came into office, according to property portal Idealista, and many Spaniards are being priced out of the cities they grew up in. In 2023, when he narrowly won re-election, Sánchez promised to add 184,000 homes to the country’s affordable housing portfolio but, having failed to pass a budget for the past three years, his government has fallen well short. Independent factcheckers say he’s only delivered around 40,000 protected homes. As he announced snap elections on October 5, the Spanish prime minister acknowledged his government had made mistakes and had not been able to deliver on all its promises, blaming a confrontational parliament and a frail coalition. “If we are to do more, we need to renew and broaden the support of the people,” he said, asking for a bigger mandate and more time. “Many injustices still need to be corrected. There are still many social goals to achieve.” After eight years at the helm, Spain’s great political survivor may struggle to convince the country to trust him with it again.

articles.title: This museum wants you to get sweaty while enjoying its art
articles.summary: Visitors to a German museum are discovering that art can not only expand their minds, but also challenge their bodies.
articles.body: Visitors to a German museum are discovering that art can not only expand their minds, but also challenge their bodies. Here, at the Kunstpalast in Düsseldorf, western Germany, art lovers are being invited to work on their fitness while enjoying the surrounding artwork. More than 70 pieces of gym equipment have been dotted around the museum, enabling art lovers to engage in workouts while taking in the surrounding paintings, sculptures and installations. Treadmills, rowing machines, cross trainers, kettlebells and more have been strategically placed so that visitors can work up a sweat in front of pieces like a 16th-century Arabian gate or a painting of Venus and Adonis by Flemish master Peter Paul Rubens. The unconventional exhibition has been launched to mark the centenary of the GeSoLei — the Exhibition for Health Care, Social Welfare and Physical Exercise, which took place in the city in 1926. Pulling in around 7.5 million people, it was the most popular exhibition of the Weimar Republic era and took place in the city’s Ehrenhof complex, which was purpose-built to house it. Today’s museum, which contains more than 800 artworks across 5,000 square meters (53,820 square feet), is located within the complex. GeSoLei covered a range of topics including medicine, sport, social welfare and nutrition and was complemented by a broad program of culture and entertainment. Entitled “GYM. Fit with Art,” the new show features a fitness circuit comprising more than 20 stations, which invite guests to build up their strength, stamina and agility. “Marking the 100th anniversary of the GeSoLei , GYM brings together two worlds that, at first glance, seem to have little in common. We’re interested in exploring what happens when we challenge our usual conceptions of a museum visit,” Felix Krämer, general director of the Kunstpalast, said in a press release. The attraction, which runs until February 21, is open to anyone who has a ticket to the museum or membership of the Urban Sports Club fitness chain, but it is down to the individual just how much effort they want to put in. There is a varied program of classes including yoga, Pilates and barre, or museum-goers can engage in their own training programs. Visitors of any age can have a go during opening hours, which run from Tuesday to Sunday — while those who prefer to take in their surroundings in a more traditional manner can continue to do so. The aim, however, is to attract new visitors who might not otherwise think to visit. Alina Fuchte, deputy head of education at the museum, told CNN: “I talked to people who said ‘I didn’t know the Kunstpalast before.’ We are a big museum in Düsseldorf and they live in the city and didn’t know the museum, but when they saw an advertisement in their gym they said, ‘Okay, I’ll try it out.’” Fuchte said there is “no pressure” to get physical, but that the initiative has proved a success so far, with all classes booking up before the exhibition actually opened on November 5. “It’s really cool to see how people actually use it and how they come in their sports dress, young and old, and really exercise in our collection,” she said. There is humor in the location of some of the stations. “Rubens is known for the bodies of women, but here Adonis has a very muscular body, a six-pack, and that’s where you can do crunches,” Fuchte said. There is a rowing machine offering a perfect view of some 19th-century seascapes, while a station by a winged altar encourages visitors to mimic that shape with chest presses. Fuchte said the exhibition is the latest in a series offering visitors a “multi-sensory experience.” “Kunstpalast in Bloom” saw florists from the city display their arrangements alongside the art, while “The Secret Power of Scent” allowed visitors to interact with it by smelling some of what they were seeing. She said the idea was to “experiment” with people’s perceptions. “We want people to come and come again, to have it as their own space, feel comfortable and see what a museum can be.” These “interventions,” as Fuchte described them, have boosted visitor numbers and “set the permanent collection in motion.” Not everyone is a fan, however. “Some people are irritated by it,” said Fuchte. “They say it doesn’t belong in the museum, or ‘why do you do that?’ But for us, it’s an offer, right? It’s an experiment. It’s not permanent and you can not use it.” There is no minimum age but children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult. Trainers are on site at the weekends and each exercise station features an explanation of how to use it, said Fuchte, who added that the museum had to take legal advice before launching the program. “We have video instructions, we have an app and we have the trainers,” she said. “That’s what we needed to do to make it safe. No one got hurt yet, so fingers crossed.”
